How much of research § 10 should spec 054 take on this PR?

options.label: Key fn + direct deltas (Recommended)
options.description: 054 takes ν as decided: `..` climbs and only an escape is refused, `\` opt-out, store-level portable opt-in. In the same PR, the deltas this forces: PATH-003, root name/parts (PATH-008/010/015), CHILD-001/003, ERR-005 (a), BE-032 A.2, 051 Layering. Resolution (§ 3.7 outcomes, BE-032 A.1 depth, ERR-005 (b)/ERR-003 widenings, the child's kⱼ, the listing rule for refused names) goes to a new item; BK-484 stays [~]. Keeps 054 one kind of spec (function, no state).

options.label: All of § 10, closes BK-484
options.description: Same, plus a Part 3 'Resolution' (state-dependent, a second spec kind in one file) and the BE-032 A.1/ERR widenings, the child kⱼ and listing decisions. One PR closes BK-468 and BK-484, but it is much larger, and #1173 already took 19 review rounds.

options.label: Only `..` and `\`
options.description: Change just the two § 9.8 differences in 054. Every other § 10 delta (root naming, child at ε, errors, portability) goes to follow-up items. Smallest PR, but 054 and specs 004/015 keep disagreeing with the research until then.

questions.question: The code refuses every `..` today (`_path.py:39`). What does this PR do about that?

options.label: Spec only, BK-469 (Recommended)
options.description: Same pattern 054 already uses: the spec states the clause, BK-469 and BL-012 record the breakage, tests that assert the old refusal are rewritten to the new clause as strict xfail, and the mark allowlist covers it. The PR stays documentation-only.

options.label: Implement the walk here
options.description: Change RemotePath's normaliser so `..` climbs, escape refused, plus tests and a user-facing CHANGELOG entry (`a/../b` becomes accepted). Ships complete for `..`, but adds code and child-store ripples to an already large PR.

questions.question: Research § 3.2/§ 3.3 makes the `\` opt-out and the portability opt-in part of the store's configuration but leaves the API shape out of scope. How does 054 state them?

options.description: 054 states each as a declared, observable store setting with its effect on ν and L_api. No API exists yet, so the clauses are allowlisted as broken today, and BK-480 widens to own the API (how to set and read both).

options.label: Defer both
options.description: 054 states only the defaults (`\` is a separator; L_api is the backend's language). The two opt-ins become a follow-up item with no clause yet. Nothing allowlisted, but the research's decisions aren't in a spec.

questions.question: What shape should spec 054 take under RFC-0024?

options.label: Abstract key layer (Recommended)
options.description: 054 states the research model in spec 051 terms only: ν (walk; `..` climbs, escape refused; step-0 refusals), ≈, acceptance (floor, backend tiers, normal-form rule, the `\` and portability opt-ins), and § 3.7's four resolution outcomes. Refusals and outcomes stay abstract; error classes and which operations accept the root are left to each operation's flow (read() first). New KEY IDs; it names PATH-002 to PATH-008 as superseded, and spec 004 gets the D7 header. Spec 051 is ground and stays untouched: its Layering pointer to 004 becomes a recorded reopen item.

options.label: Keep 054's 0.33 anchoring
options.description: Keep moved PATH IDs, `InvalidPath`, the Store method lists and the BE-0xx links; fix only `..`, `\` and resolution. Less rewriting, but it contradicts R1 (054 could never become ground) and D7 (PATH-003 would change meaning under the same ID).

questions.question: What evidence ships with the spec?

options.label: Formal + reference model (Recommended)
options.description: Like spec 051: BK-484's Lean proofs move into `sdd/formal/lean/` beside StoreAxioms.lean, and the spike becomes a reference-model test in `tests/` carrying the KEY marks (as `test_store_tree.py` does for 051). The 0.33-targeted tests from #1171 (`test_store_keys.py`, the KEY-009 Windows xfail, the mark allowlists) are dropped: comparing with 0.33 is D8's later pass. On acceptance, the spec and model join the ground register.

options.label: Spec only
options.description: The Lean proofs and spike stay under `sdd/research/` as review aids, and every KEY ID is allowlisted in the mark gate. A smaller PR, but no formal model is accepted, so by research § 3 the spec can't join the ground.

questions.question: What happens to #1171's parts that bind 0.33 code or the kernel?

options.label: Strip them (Recommended)
options.description: Remove RFC-0023 (kernel/driver design is class P, paused by R2) and the CLAUDE.md 'Kernel migration' paragraph (it contradicts the pause). BL-012 is decided against (D9 already rules out a release). BK-469 becomes 'the key layer's D8 comparison with 0.33', which creates `sdd/v1-breaks.md`. BK-480 becomes class F (a v1 API choice). RFC-0023's content survives as a note in a paused item's dossier.

options.label: Keep, marked paused
options.description: RFC-0023 stays in the PR as a Draft whose status says 'paused (RFC-0024)'. BK-469 and BL-012 are kept and re-labelled class P. Less churn, but it lands kernel design during a freeze and keeps a release blocker D9 makes redundant.

questions.question: How does 054 record how backends differ?

options.label: D6 profile tables (Recommended)
options.description: 054 names abstract axes (separator `\`, name characters, name and key length with unit, trailing rewrite, reserved names, segment count, name equality). A table beside the spec gives Memory, Local, S3 and SFTP per axis, each cell citing research-backend-path-authorities.md or the 2026-10-22 probes. This replaces KEY-008's 'profile declared in the backend's spec'.

options.label: Keep KEY-008's profiles
options.description: The four named profiles stay in the clause, with no per-backend table. Against D6, and the backend facts stay scattered across the research docs.

Research § 2 sets Σ to the Unicode scalar values, so a surrogate is never a name. But step 0 lists only NUL and an opted-out `\` as raw-input refusals. Should `\ud800/..` (a surrogate in a segment the walk later drops) be refused?

options.label: Refuse anywhere (Recommended)
options.description: A surrogate joins step 0: refused wherever it appears in the input, as NUL is. It is the same reasoning as § 5's NUL row: no input carrying a code point outside Σ denotes a key. The spike and Lean add one case each.

options.label: Only in the result
options.description: Only a surrogate that survives the walk is refused, by the floor, so `\ud800/..` reduces to ε. This keeps step 0 exactly as researched, but an input with a non-Σ code point can denote the root, the case § 5 calls a defect for NUL.
